correctness.rationale: Marking the occurrence of each even part 2m in the distinct-even Euler product gives qB'(q)−4B(q)Σm q^(2m)/(1+q^(2m)), with B the b4 series. Modulo 2 the two factors of the correction are the triangular-number series (Jacobi's cubic identity) and the square/twice-square series at exponents 2a² and 4a² (parity of σ). The change x=2j+1, y=4a is a bijection with the required positive form representations. For M=8n+1 a prime p≡5,7 mod 8 to odd valuation rules out x²+2y²; the signed ordered x²+y² count is 8R1+4·1_square. In the nonzero sum-of-two-squares case all 3 mod 4 prime exponents are even, so an odd exponent of a 5 mod 8 prime forces a second such prime, making the divisor sum a multiple of 4 and R1 even. A 7 mod 8 prime instead forces R1=0. The progression residues have valuation exactly one at 5 or 7 respectively. The inspected b4 theorems have precisely the required progressions and stronger moduli. At n=0 both form counts vanish; at n=2 the correction is nontrivial (M=17, R1=1, W(2)=0 while n b4(n)=4). Independent direct partition/form enumeration verified 0≤n≤30 (record3_bounded_check.py and .txt); the supplied 2401-index and other reported checks were inspected as recorded evidence, not rerun or treated as proof.

value.rationale: The correction supplies an all-index, nontrivial arithmetic description for an existing signed partition statistic; it does more than produce ten isolated residues or repeat a partition-count identity. The odd-valuation criterion explains when congruences for the unweighted count transfer to the weighted mass and applies without assuming a fixed progression. The ten progressions demonstrate that mechanism rather than carrying the value on their own.
